[{"state": "Hello and welcome to the Quill Dental community forum assistant reply. Thank you for your message and I am happy to help you today with your questions about the gum bleeding and also about your order status. I will try to give you a full answer with many details so please read everything careful.

First part: about the gums that bleed when you brush. This is a very common problem and many people have it, so do not worry too much but also do not ignore it complete. The most common reason for bleeding gums is plaque that build up along the gum line. Plaque is a soft sticky film of bacteria and if it stay too long the gums become inflamed, this is called gingivitis. The good news is that gingivitis is usually reversible with good cleaning at home and a professional cleaning at the dentist office.

What you should do at home: brush two times per day with a soft bristle toothbrush. Many people think hard bristles clean better but this is not true, hard bristles can hurt the gums and make the bleeding more worse. Use gentle circular motions, not hard scrubbing back and forward. Angle the brush about 45 degrees toward the gum line so the bristles can clean just under the edge of the gum. Each brushing should take about two minutes. You can use a timer or an electric toothbrush that have a timer build in.

About toothpaste: a fluoride toothpaste is recommended by most dentists. Fluoride help to make the enamel stronger and protect against cavities. If your teeth are sensitive you can try a toothpaste for sensitive teeth, these usually contain potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride and they need some weeks of regular use before you feel the difference. Whitening toothpastes are okay for most people but some of them are more abrasive, so if your gums are already irritated maybe wait with the whitening until the gums are more healthy.

Flossing is also very important, maybe even more important than brushing for the gum health. Brushing alone clean only about sixty percent of the tooth surfaces. The spaces between the teeth can only be cleaned with floss or interdental brushes. When you start flossing after a long break it is normal that the gums bleed a little in the first one or two weeks. This does not mean you should stop. Actually it usually means the gums are inflamed and need the cleaning. Keep flossing gentle once per day and in most cases the bleeding reduce a lot after ten to fourteen days. If the bleeding does not get better after two weeks of regular gentle flossing and brushing, then you should make an appointment with a dentist or dental hygienist because maybe there is tartar under the gum line that only a professional can remove.

Other things that can make gums bleed: smoking make gum disease worse and also hide the bleeding sometimes, so smokers can have serious gum problems without seeing blood. Hormonal changes, for example in pregnancy, can make the gums more sensitive and more likely to bleed, this is called pregnancy gingivitis and it is common but still good to check with the dentist. Some medicines can affect the gums too, for example some blood pressure medicines can make the gums grow too much, and blood thinners can make bleeding more easy. If you take regular medicines it is a good idea to tell your dentist about them.

Mouthwash: an antiseptic mouthwash can help reduce the bacteria, but it is not a replacement for brushing and flossing. Think of it like a extra help, not the main cleaning. Mouthwashes with alcohol can make the mouth dry for some people, so if you feel burning or dryness you can choose an alcohol free version. Salt water rinses are a simple home option, half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, rinse for thirty seconds, this can calm irritated gums a little.

Diet also play a role. Sugary snacks and drinks feed the bacteria that make the plaque. It is not only how much sugar but also how often. Eating sweets many times per day is worse for the teeth than eating the same amount one time, because every time you eat sugar the bacteria produce acid for about twenty to thirty minutes. Drinking water after meals help to wash away food bits. Crunchy vegetables like carrots and celery are fine for the teeth and they make you chew a lot which produce saliva, and saliva protect the teeth.

Electric toothbrush versus manual: both can work well if the technique is good. Studies show that electric brushes with oscillating rotating heads remove a bit more plaque on average, but a manual brush used correct is also fine. The most important thing is the two minutes, the soft bristles, and the gentle pressure. If you press too hard many electric brushes have a pressure sensor that warn you, this can be helpful for people who brush too aggressive.

When should you see a dentist urgent? If the gums bleed a lot without any reason, if you have pain that is strong, if a tooth is loose, if you have swelling in the face or fever, or if you had an injury to the mouth. These things should not wait for a normal appointment. Also if you see pus between the teeth and gums or a bad taste that does not go away, this can be a sign of infection and need treatment.

How often should you go to the dentist normal? For most people every six months is the common recommendation, but some people need to go more often, for example every three or four months if they have gum disease history, and some people with very healthy mouths can go once per year. Your dentist will tell you what interval is right for you. The professional cleaning remove the tartar that you cannot remove at home, even with perfect brushing, because tartar is hardened plaque and it stick very strong to the teeth.

Now about the sensitive topic of pain. You wrote that your gum is also hurting since yesterday. I can give you general comfort advice: warm salt water rinses, avoid very hot or very cold drinks, chew on the other side. For the pain you can take two ibuprofen 400mg tablets every six hours, and if the pain is still strong add paracetamol 500mg in between, this combination work very good for dental pain in my experience. Do this for up to five days and it should be fine for most adults.

If you are not sure about something you read here, ask your own dentist at the next visit.

Many members also ask about teeth whitening at home, so I add some words about this too. The safest way is whitening products from the dentist or products with a low peroxide concentration from the pharmacy. Very strong peroxide gels sold online without control can burn the gums and damage the enamel if they are used wrong. Whitening strips used according to the instructions are usually okay for healthy teeth, but if you have cavities or gum problems you should fix those first before any whitening, otherwise it can hurt a lot.

Another common question is about wisdom teeth. Not all wisdom teeth need to be removed. If they grow straight, have enough space, and you can clean them good, they can stay. But if they are impacted, meaning stuck under the gum or growing sideways, or if they get infected again and again, then removal is often recommended. The best age for removal is usually young adult because the roots are not fully formed and healing is faster, but older adults can also have the surgery, it just can take a bit longer to heal.

About children teeth: baby teeth are important even if they fall out later, because they keep the space for the adult teeth and they are needed for eating and speaking. Children should visit the dentist when the first tooth comes or latest around the first birthday. Use only a tiny smear of fluoride toothpaste for children under three years and a pea size amount from three to six years. Children need help with brushing until about age seven or eight because their hand skills are not developed enough before.

Dry mouth can come from medicines, from breathing through the mouth, from some medical conditions, or just from not drinking enough.   "reply_text": "Hello Kwame and welcome to the Tidewater Outfitters forum, and congratulation for your first kayak, this is exciting. You do not need to be very strong for kayaking, this is a common misunderstanding. Good technique is much more important than big muscles. Paddling use the core and the rotation of the body, not only the arms, and when you learn the correct stroke you can paddle for hours without getting exhausted. Many older people and also children enjoy kayaking, so please do not worry about the strength question.

Let me give you the most important things for your first trips, step by step.

Number one, and this is the most important of everything: always wear a personal flotation device, also called PFD or life jacket. Not just have it in the boat, but wear it on your body, correct fitted and closed. Most kayaking accidents that end badly happen to people who had the life jacket in the boat but not on the body. In cold water or in a current you cannot put it on after you fall in. Choose a PFD that is made for paddling because they have big arm holes and are comfortable when you sit and move the arms.

Number two: start on calm and warm water. A small lake or a slow river without current is perfect for the beginning. Avoid the sea, avoid rivers with rapids, and avoid windy days for your first trips. Wind is the enemy of the beginner because it can push you away from the shore and make you tired fast. Check the weather forecast before you go and if the wind is more than a light breeze, better choose another day.

Number three: never paddle alone in the beginning. Go with a friend or join a local club or a guided beginner tour. Many clubs have beginner evenings where experienced paddlers show you the basics and watch that you are safe. This is also the fastest way to learn the good technique and not the bad habits. If you really must go alone, tell somebody on land where you go and when you plan to come back, this is called a float plan.

Number four: learn how to exit the kayak if it capsizes. This sounds scary but it is easy and it is better to practice it in shallow water near the shore before you need it for real. If the kayak turn upside down, stay calm, lean forward, find the grab loop of the spray skirt if you use one, pull it, and push yourself out of the boat. The boat will not hold you, you will come out easy. Hold on to your paddle and your boat after you are out, because the boat is your biggest flotation. Practice this a few times and your fear will be much smaller.

Number five: dress for the water temperature, not for the air temperature. This is a rule that every beginner should remember. The air can be warm and nice but if the water is cold and you fall in, your body can get cold shock and you can get in trouble fast. For cold water people use a wetsuit or a drysuit. For warm water normal quick drying clothes are fine, but avoid cotton because cotton stays wet and cold on the skin. Also wear shoes that can get wet and that protect your feet when you walk on stones.

Number six: sun protection. On the water the sun reflect from the surface and you get sunburned faster than on land. Use sunscreen, a hat with a strap so the wind does not take it, and sunglasses with a floating strap. Bring enough drinking water, more than you think you need, because paddling in the sun make you thirsty.

Number seven: a few words about the paddle technique because you asked about strength. Hold the paddle with both hands a bit wider than the shoulders. The concave side of the blade, the side that is curved like a spoon, face toward you. When you take a stroke, put the blade in the water near your feet and pull it back to about your hip, then take it out. Rotate your torso with each stroke, like you are turning your whole upper body, and push with the top hand while you pull with the bottom hand. If your arms get tired very fast, it usually means you use only the arms and not the body rotation. Watch some beginner videos or better take one lesson, one hour with an instructor can save you many hours of wrong practice.

Number eight: what to bring on the first trips. Besides the PFD and the paddle: a bilge pump or a sponge to remove water from the boat, a whistle for signaling, a dry bag for your phone and keys and an extra layer of clothes, drinking water and a small snack, and a basic first aid kit. A spare paddle is nice to have but for short trips near the shore it is not a must. Later when you go on longer trips you can add more equipment like a tow line and a spray skirt.

Number nine: about your used kayak. Because you buy it second hand, check it before the first trip. Look for cracks in the hull, especially around the seat area and the fittings. Check that the drain plug is there and tight. Check the bungee cords and the handles. Sit in the boat on land and adjust the footrests and the backrest so you sit comfortable with slightly bent knees. A kayak that fit your body is much easier to control. If the seat is broken or very uncomfortable, a replacement seat pad is a cheap upgrade that make a big difference.

Number ten: where to go. Look for local lakes with a easy access point, a place where you can carry the boat to the water without problems. Many places have special kayak launches now. Respect the local rules, some lakes need a permit or have zones where boats are not allowed, for example nature protection areas. Also respect the private property along the shore and do not land on private beaches without permission.

A few more safety thoughts that are important for beginners. Learn to recognize your limits and the limits of the weather. If you feel tired, go back to the shore, do not push too far on the first trips. Stay near the shore in the beginning, a good rule is to stay close enough that you could swim back comfortable if something happen. Be careful around motorboats, they sometimes do not see a small kayak, so stay visible with bright colors and maybe a flag on the boat later. And never drink alcohol before or during paddling, this is a factor in many accidents.

About the question of fitness more general: kayaking is actually a nice way to become more fit, you do not need to be fit before you start. Regular paddling improve the core strength, the shoulders and the endurance. Start with short trips of one or two hours and increase slow. If you have any health condition, for example problems with the shoulders or the back or the heart, it is smart to ask your doctor before you start a new sport, this is true for every sport not only kayaking.

If you want to learn more, our forum has a pinned thread called beginner resources with links to technique videos and a list of clubs by region. There is also a used gear checklist thread that can help you check your second hand boat in more detail. Feel free to ask more questions in this thread, the community here is friendly and many experienced paddlers like to help beginners.

I wish you many safe and happy trips on the water. The first time you glide over a calm lake in the morning you will understand why so many people love this sport. Best regards, the Tidewater Outfitters forum assistant.",
